name: Terraform configuration
description: The Terraform configuration in the checkout: every root directory holding `.tf` files, the backend it stores state in, the providers and modules it takes on and how tightly they are pinned, the resources it declares, the variables it takes, the lock file that resolves it, and any state file left in the tree. Everything is read from the files themselves, so it works on a runner with no Terraform installed. When the `terraform` CLI is there, the versions an initialised root has already resolved are added.

directory.description: Directory the configuration is looked for under, relative to the directory the CLI runs in. By default discovery walks the whole working directory; this only narrows it, so a repository that keeps its Terraform in one place collects just that place.

terraform.description: Terraform CLI, run only to read back the provider versions an already initialised root resolved. Never `init`, `plan` or `apply`, so nothing it does reaches real infrastructure.
terraform.remediation: Install with `brew install terraform`, or add the `hashicorp/setup-terraform` step to the workflow. The configuration is read out of the files either way, so this only adds the resolved versions.

facts.directory: The directory set by the guardrail's `directory` input, relative to the directory the CLI runs in. Every other path this collector reports is also relative to the directory the CLI runs in, so it resolves from where you invoked the CLI, not from wherever the collector happened to run.
facts.source: `report` when the configuration was read out of the checkout, `tool` when `terraform` was also run against an initialised root, `none` when there is no Terraform here at all.
facts.reason: Why nothing was found, present only when `source` is `none`.
facts.reports: Every configuration file that was read and understood, in path order. A file the reader could not handle is in `unparsed` instead.
facts.reports[].path: Path of the file, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.
facts.reports[].modified: When the file was last written, ISO 8601.
facts.reports[].format: What it was read as: `tf`, `tfvars` or `lock`.
facts.tool.name: `terraform`, present only when it was run.
facts.tool.version: Version of the `terraform` on the runner.
facts.tool.args: Arguments of the last invocation. `providers -json` is tried first and `version -json` is the fallback, because only the second is supported by every release.
facts.roots: Every directory holding at least one `.tf` file, in path order. A reusable module directory counts as one too, so keep that in mind when reading `backend.type` on a root that is not live.
facts.roots[].path: Directory of the root, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.
facts.roots[].backend.type: Backend the root stores state in, as the `backend` label names it. `local` when the root declares no backend block at all, which is itself a finding, not a default to ignore.
facts.roots[].backend.attributes: Every attribute the backend block declares, by name. A value is carried only when it is a plain scalar the reader could resolve; anything interpolated, structured or named like a credential is `null`, so the key shows the attribute is set without the secret becoming evidence too.
facts.roots[].backend.encrypted: Whether the backend declares its state encrypted, from `encrypt` or a key attribute for the backends that have one. `null` when the backend says nothing either way, which is not the same as `false`.
facts.roots[].backend.locking: Whether the backend declares state locking, from `use_lockfile`, `dynamodb_table`, `lock` or `lock_address` depending on the backend. `null` when the backend says nothing either way.
facts.roots[].providers: Every provider the root requires, from `required_providers` first and then any `provider` block naming one that was not required.
facts.roots[].providers[].name: Local name of the provider, as the configuration refers to it.
facts.roots[].providers[].source: Source address as written, such as `hashicorp/aws`, or `null` when only a `provider` block names it.
facts.roots[].providers[].version: Version constraint exactly as written, such as `~> 6.0`, or `null` when none is declared.
facts.roots[].providers[].pinned: Whether that constraint pins one exact version. A `~>`, a range, or no constraint at all is not pinned.
facts.roots[].modules: Every `module` block the root declares, in the order the files declare them.
facts.roots[].modules[].name: Label of the module block.
facts.roots[].modules[].source: Its `source` exactly as written, or `null` when the source is interpolated rather than literal.
facts.roots[].modules[].version: Its `version` constraint, which only a registry source can carry, or `null`.
facts.roots[].modules[].local: Whether the source is a relative path inside the repository, so nothing is fetched.
facts.roots[].modules[].registry: Whether the source is a module registry address, meaning `version` is what pins it.
facts.roots[].modules[].git: Whether the source is a git or HTTP URL, meaning the ref in the URL is what pins it and `version` never applies.
facts.roots[].resources: How many `resource` blocks the root declares, by resource type. `data` blocks are not counted.
facts.roots[].variables: Every `variable` block the root declares. Names only: a default can be a credential and these facts are attached to the build as evidence.
facts.roots[].variables[].name: Label of the variable block.
facts.roots[].variables[].hasDefault: Whether it declares a `default` at all. The default itself is never collected.
facts.roots[].varFiles: Every `.tfvars` file committed beside the root.
facts.roots[].varFiles[].path: Path of the file, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.
facts.roots[].varFiles[].variables: The variable names it assigns, sorted. The values are never collected.
facts.roots[].lockfile.path: Path of that lock file, relative to the directory the CLI runs in, or `null` when there is none.
facts.roots[].lockfile.providers: Every provider the lock file resolves.
facts.roots[].lockfile.providers[].name: Last segment of the provider address, matching the local name in the usual case.
facts.roots[].lockfile.providers[].source: Full address the lock file names, such as `registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws`, so a mirror is recognisable.
facts.roots[].lockfile.providers[].hashes: How many hashes it records. Only the count is kept, not the hashes, because the count is what shows whether the lock covers more than one platform.
facts.roots[].unparsed: How many files in this root the reader could not handle. Above zero, this root is described from only part of its configuration, so treat an absence here as unknown, not as a finding.
facts.stateFiles: Every `.tfstate` or `.tfstate.backup` file left in the tree, which is a finding in itself. The walk skips `.terraform`, so a working directory Terraform manages is not one of these.
facts.stateFiles[].path: Path of the state file, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.
facts.stateFiles[].bytes: Its size in bytes. The contents are never read.
facts.unparsed: Every file the reader could not handle, so a guardrail can tell a configuration that says nothing apart from one that could not be read.
facts.unparsed[].path: Path of that file, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.
facts.unparsed[].reason: Why the reader could not handle it.
facts.resolved: Provider versions an initialised root has already resolved, read back with `terraform`. Present only when the tool is on the runner and the root carries a `.terraform/providers` directory, which is what `terraform init` leaves behind and what tells an initialised root from a stale one.
facts.resolved[].root: Root the versions were read in.
facts.resolved[].name: Last segment of the provider address.
facts.resolved[].source: Full provider address as Terraform names it.
